verdicts.quote: “Use the secretKey of your API key as the signing key for the HMAC-SHA-256 algorithm.”
verdicts.reason: Binance’s REST API uses API keys with request signing; HMAC-SHA256 signing is explicitly documented and is the standard way to authenticate signed endpoints.

verdicts.quote: “before creating an API key, you need to… complete identity verification.”
verdicts.reason: Developers can self-serve API keys from their account after free signup/KYC; no paid plan or app review is required. A free Spot Testnet is also available for testing.

verdicts.quote: “Explore… across every Binance product — 38 products, 1113 endpoints.”
verdicts.reason: The catalog shows extensive coverage across Spot, Futures, Options, Margin, Wallet, Earn, VIP/Institutional, etc., indicating a broad API surface.

verdicts.quote: “The Binance MCP Server is an MCP (Model Context Protocol) endpoint that lets MCP‑compatible AI agents connect to Binance”
verdicts.reason: This is an official Binance Support article describing Binance’s own MCP server.

verdicts.quote: “By default, an API key cannot ‘TRADE’. You need to enable trading in API Management first.”
verdicts.reason: It’s buildable now with self-serve keys and docs, but practical use has caveats: KYC, permission toggles (e.g., enable trading), and typical exchange rate-limit/security controls.
